 사진 확대 The Bithumb Lounge in Seocho-gu, Seoul, is reportedly considering various measures, weighing the direction of suspending taxation on virtual assets, which is scheduled to take effect in January next year. [Yonhap News] In addition, the Democratic Party of Korea decided to decide its position as soon as possible after collecting additional opinions from the party on whether to suspend taxation on virtual assets.
 Democratic Party floor spokesman Jeon Eun-soo met with reporters after a general meeting of lawmakers at the National Assembly on the 27th and said, "We will collect a little more opinions and make it possible to decide."
 "There were opinions that the contents that actually went back and forth (from the assembly) should be postponed," said Kwon Chil-seung, chairman of the policy committee, who delivered various opinions on the taxation of virtual assets at the assembly.
 Referring to the opinion expressed by Rep. Ahn Do-gul on the Democratic Party's YouTube broadcast "Minti07," he added, "He said (the argument) that it would be appropriate to enact the Digital Basic Asset Act and implement it together, and opinions to that extent were divided (in the parliamentary assembly)."
 "That doesn't mean that (the party) has been decided today," he said, adding, "We will remain about 60 days from the implementation of (virtual asset taxation) so that we can make a decision as soon as possible."
 Meanwhile, virtual asset taxation has been suspended three times since the introduction of the related system in 2020. If no additional moratorium is made, taxation will take effect in January next year.
 The taxable amount is 2.5 million won minus the basic deduction from the annual income generated by the transfer and loan of virtual assets. On top of that, a 22% tax rate is applied, including other income taxes and local income taxes.
